# ARGUS 2027 build progress

The build session's log. Feature and gate status live in `docs/build/features.json`; read them with `python3 tools/build_ledger.py summary`. The live copies of both files are on the integration branch `platform/build-2027`; `main` keeps the starting copies until the build ends. How the session works is in `docs/build/SESSION.md`.

## Decisions made during the build

Choices the specs did not settle, with the reason. Newest first.

| Date | Feature | Decision | Why |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-11-18 | SIM-03 | What the spec's wind numbers mean here. `gust_mps` is the standard deviation of the gusts along the mean wind; gusts across it are half that and vertical gusts three tenths. Each is an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process with one correlation time per flight, drawn from 2 to 5 s by the scenario's seed. The discrete gust is one (1 - cos) pulse of the set peak, 4 s long, starting 20 to 60 s after the wind starts. `direction_deg` is the bearing the wind comes from. A payload's drag area is 1.05 times its largest face and a bucket's is its diameter times its height | "4 m/s with 1 m/s gusts" does not say what the 1 m/s is, how gusts split between directions, or when the discrete gust comes. A standard deviation is the usual reading; the seed makes a flight's wind repeatable. All are constants in `sim/wind_model.py` and `sim/wind.py` |
| 2026-11-18 | SIM-03 | The force is given to Gazebo as its change since the last update, and every 5 s the accumulated changes are cleared and the whole force sent again once the clear has been taken (10 ms of sim time). A body's velocity is its true pose differenced over 0.1 s. Only a windy scenario's world is built with the ApplyLinkWrench system | Gazebo's persistent wrenches add up: a second message for the same body is applied as well as the first (checked in the gz-sim 8 source), and the one-step wrench would act for a millisecond in every fifty. Sending changes keeps the sum equal to the force wanted; the periodic clear keeps the pile short. Gazebo publishes poses, not velocities. A calm run's world must stay the base world, for the flags-off baseline |
| 2026-11-18 | SIM-03 | The pass line is a scored flight, `hover/wind_5`: a new driver (`sim/hover.py`) takes off to 10 m and holds for 40 s in a steady 5 m/s wind, a new `hover` judge checks it held within 3 m, and the tilt is judged from the wind tool's own record: the mean tilt over the updates where the vehicle was above 2 m and slower than 0.5 m/s (at least 100 of them) against atan(mean force / mg), within 20%. The vehicle's mass is 1.755 kg, the sum of its links in the sim's models. A windy mission flight is not held to the tilt line, only to the wind having blown (`wind.json`); without that record the run is INVALID | "Hovering at 5 m/s wind, logged tilt within 20% of atan(F / mg)" needs a hover, a force and a mass. No 2026 mission hovers for long, and a new sequence file would be a new shipped config. The force and the tilt come from the same tool and the same updates, so they are compared like with like |
| 2026-11-18 | SIM-09, FND-01, FND-03 | The 260 to 275 ms frame age at the 95th percentile seen in wave 1 is the 2026 detector's queue, not the camera, the bridge or the publish. On one recorded `delivery/baseline` flight, flags off: render 0.7 ms, bridge 14 ms, detector 19 ms, publish 0.2 ms at the median; at the 95th percentile 1.9, 17.7, 213 and 0.8 ms (frame age 35 ms median, 228 ms at the 95th percentile). Likely cause: below about 6 m the bullseye is large in the image and the detector's work per frame goes past the 33 ms between frames (57 to 59 ms at the 95th percentile, bursts to 187 ms), and its image subscription keeps five frames and takes the oldest first, so once it is behind, every detection is of a frame that has waited 150 to 270 ms. Nothing in the 2026 detector is changed. For the lead: the 2027 detector node and camera driver should take the newest frame and drop the rest (a queue of one) | Asked for by the lead during the session. Above 6 m nothing waits (waiting 0 to 3 ms at the 95th percentile); the detector's work is flat from 18 m to 6 m, so the two debug images it publishes each frame are not the cause; and with a 1.5 m bullseye, small in the image until the last 3 m, the 95th percentile of the frame age falls from 228 ms to 98 ms. What inside the detector's work grows with the target's size was not separated: that needs the detector instrumented. `docs/results/2026-11-18-frame-age-by-stage.md` |
| 2026-11-18 | SIM-09 | The replay reads bags without ROS: its own CDR codec and a table of the layouts of the recorded types (`sim/replay/msgdefs.py`), checked against the installed messages by `sim/replay/check_defs.py` wherever ROS is (33 of 33 match in the sim image). It reads rosbag2's sqlite3 storage and MCAP. The sim's recorder uses MCAP when the plugin is installed and sqlite3 otherwise; the sim image has no MCAP plugin and the session did not rebuild the image, so every bag recorded in the session is sqlite3 and the MCAP reader has only read files written by the replay's own writer | CI has no ROS, and the spec asks for `core` in pure Python on bags the tests generate. Rebuilding the image re-runs its `apt` and `rosdep` steps, which could bring newer MAVROS or Gazebo packages into the baseline that gate G0-W2 is about to re-check; that is the lead's call. `rosbag2_storage_mcap` is now an `exec_depend` of `drone_utils`, so the next `sim/run_sim.sh --build` installs it |
| 2026-11-18 | SIM-09 | What of the spec's recording list is left out, and why. Flow frames: there is no flow camera or flow code yet (SIM-05 brings the sim's camera; the flow lane the code); they are images, so they will be tapped, not stored. 4K frames as JPEG files with an index: `argus_camera`'s `FrameLog` is the writer, and nothing constructs it yet outside its tests; the recorder does not write frames. The error at the release: nothing in the bag marks the release, so `core` takes the time by hand (`--release-ns`) until servo outputs are recorded (SIM-06). On the aircraft the launch file taps no image topic unless told to, and the player (`play.launch.py`) keeps recorded setpoints under `/recorded/...` always and does not start while a MAVROS is live in the ROS domain | spec-auditor: each of these was missing without being said. flight-guardian: a tap on `/camera/image` makes the 2026 grabber publish raw frames it otherwise does not, upstream of the detector, and a bag played beside a live vehicle would put recorded setpoints and poses on MAVROS's topics. The sim's `--record` still taps: it is how the frame age was measured |
| 2026-11-18 | SIM-09 | "Lost-state duration" is the time the class's primary track is LOST, to the end of the bag (`lost_state_s`). `without_lock_after_first_lock_s` is kept beside it: the time without a CONFIRMED track between the first lock and the last. The sim's `--record` runs `ros2 bag record` through `sim/replay/record_run.py`, a runner side tool, not through `record.launch.py`; both build the command with the same function. The bag reader imports `zstandard` or `lz4` only if a file's chunks are compressed that way and says how to record without when they are missing; neither is needed for anything the session records | The spec names the metric and not its definition; a loss that is never made good must count. The runner starts side tools as scripts with the run folder as their argument. The two modules are outside the allowed list for ROS-free code, so their use is optional and guarded, as SESSION.md asks |
| 2026-11-18 | SIM-09 | Servo outputs are not recorded yet, though the spec lists them. MAVROS publishes them (`/mavros/rc/out`) from its `rc_io` plugin, which `config/mavros/argus_mavros.yaml` does not load, and the repo's own guard (`test_stream_keeper.py`) holds the loaded plugins to exactly the ones used | Loading `rc_io` also opens MAVROS's RC-override input and needs a message rate from the stream keeper: a change to the flight's MAVROS configuration, made for a recorder. SIM-06's payload bridge is the first thing that reads servo outputs and settles how they reach ROS; the topic joins `sim/replay/topics.py` then |
| 2026-11-18 | SIM-09 | Images are not recorded. The bag gets one `std_msgs/Header` per frame seen on an image topic (`/replay/frame_seen/<topic>`, cut from the front of the serialised image without unpacking it), and on a sim run on wall time Gazebo's clock on `/replay/sim_clock`. In the sim `--record` on `sim/run_scenarios.sh` records any scenario into its run folder | The spec keeps frames out of the bag ("4K frames stay as JPEG files with an index"); a raw 640 x 360 stream alone is 20 MB a second and would slow the flight it records. The header is enough to say when each frame arrived, which is what the latency metrics need |
| 2026-11-18 | SIM-09 | `core` replays the estimator only: it is the only one of "the estimator, tracker and flow code" that exists. It steps the feed at each detection's recorded arrival time and reads the tracks every 100 ms of bag time, as the executor's timer does. The `ros` mode is `play.launch.py`: `ros2 bag play --clock` with every recorded topic but the flight's own `/clock`, and the flight's outputs (detections, tracks, setpoints) under `/recorded/...`; it does not replay frames, since none are in the bag | Flow velocity error and per-marker localisation error are added with the flow code and LOC-7. A player that publishes the driver's JPEG frame log as images belongs with the first field bag (G7) |
| 2026-11-18 | FND-07 | `may_descend` and `may_release` take an optional `track_id` and then answer about that track only ("gone" if it no longer exists); the `Permission` names the track it is about. `height_agl()` gives nothing when the newest pose is more than 0.5 s from now. `latlon_to_local_enu` pairs the GPS fix with the local position of the fix's own moment (the pose history when it is on, otherwise the newest pose if within 0.25 s of the fix) and gives nothing for a fix whose status says no fix, a fix over 2 s old, or no pose of that moment | flight-guardian: asked by class, the rules could say yes about a second red object while the target being flown to is lost; a stalled pose stream would leave the last height standing as the input to a release-height gate; and a fix 0.2 s older than the pose shifts the converted point 0.8 m at survey speed. The three limits (0.5 s, 2 s, 0.25 s) are new numbers, not 2026 tuning |
| 2026-11-18 | FND-07 | For the lead: with FND-06's numbers the 0.5 s limit for descending never binds. A CONFIRMED track becomes COASTING 0.3 s after its last hit, and COASTING does not permit a descent, so both rules refuse from 0.3 s. If a descent was meant to ride through a gap of 0.3 to 0.5 s, either COASTING must permit it or the coast time must be 0.5 s: a spec change, not made here | spec-auditor and flight-guardian both noted it. The code follows both spec lines to the letter and errs to the strict side. In the sim a frame is 40 ms old at the median but 260 to 275 ms at the 95th percentile, so the 0.3 s edge is close: see the frame-age breakdown under SIM-09 |
| 2026-11-18 | FND-07 | The two rules are context calls, `may_descend(cls)` and `may_release(cls)`, that return a `Permission` (true or false, with the reason). Both need a CONFIRMED track: the spec asks for CONFIRMED only for descending, and "a track no older than 0.3 s" for releasing | "Rules enforced here, not in each mission" needs a call a mission can ask. For releasing, a track 0.3 s old or less can only be CONFIRMED or TENTATIVE (a CONFIRMED track coasts after 0.3 s), and releasing on a target seen once or twice is not what the rule is for; the stricter reading is the safe one and costs nothing when the track is good. An age that is not a number, or more than 50 ms negative, permits nothing |
| 2026-11-18 | FND-07 | `height_agl()` is the vehicle's height minus projection v2's rangefinder ground when that is healthy (source `rangefinder`), otherwise the height above home (source `baro`). `latlon_to_local_enu` adds the offset from the vehicle's own latitude and longitude to its local position, with ArduPilot's own scale (111 318.845 m per degree, longitude by the cosine of the middle latitude). `estimator_ready()` is true when the estimator is attached and the pose history can place a frame taken now. `primary_target(cls, near=None)` takes an optional point to choose among equal tracks | CEN-03 builds `height_estimator.py` (the 15 degree tilt limit, the ground offset on baro) and `height_agl()` will pass that on; until then this is what exists, and it already says which source it used. The tracks live in ArduPilot's local frame, so a coordinate is put into it the way ArduPilot would, and anchoring on the vehicle needs no home position. A drop mission's bullseye is the one near its GPS target, hence `near` |
| 2026-11-18 | FND-06 | Limits on the estimator's work inside the executor: at most 16 detections of one frame are used (the most confident of each class, class by class in turn, so a crowd of one class cannot push out the one detection of another), at most 4 frames are handled per step, the rest waiting for the next; a frame leaves the queue before it is handled, so one that makes the estimator fail is counted and dropped once; every callback is guarded. When the clock steps back more than 0.5 s, every track that ever confirmed becomes LOST as of now and the rest are dropped. Detections from the 2026 detector are used only once it has said what size its image is (the estimator keeps its own copy from `/drone_package_drop/image_size`, because the missions clear the executor's between missions) and only while that size is the calibrated mode's. On this laptop a step costs 0.2 ms with one bullseye and 12 ms at the bounds (`python3 tools/estimator_step_cost.py`) | flight-guardian: the estimator shares the executor's one thread with the 20 Hz tick, so its work per callback must be bounded and its faults must not reach the tick or replay frames into the filter; a track whose last hit lies in the future would read as just seen; and the 2026 grabbers can send a reduced image, whose pixels the mode's calibration does not describe (the mission path already refuses that). Other detectors do not say what size they ran on and are taken at the contract's word |
| 2026-11-18 | FND-06 | How the sim acceptance lines are judged (`sim/estimator_check.py`): each time the tracks are published (10 Hz) the oldest CONFIRMED bullseye track is compared with the truth; a line is the 95th percentile of those errors while the vehicle is within 1.5 m of 15 m, 1.0 m of 6 m and 0.4 m of 2.4 m, with at least 20 such samples. Samples in a band with no CONFIRMED track are not errors; they are counted by state (`states`, `without_a_confirmed_track`) in the report so a band that passed on few samples shows it | The spec gives the three numbers and no rule. The vehicle passes the bands again on the climb-out and the return, when nothing is being looked at, so "no track" cannot count as an error; counting it by state keeps a track that was missing while the mission was looking visible to whoever reads the report. In the flight that counts every sample on the way down was CONFIRMED |
| 2026-11-18 | FND-06 | A detection whose box (taken as centred on the detection's centre) comes within 2 px of the image's edge is not given to the filter; it is counted (`skipped: box cut by the image's edge`). A target that is only cut-off boxes, such as one that fills the frame, therefore coasts and is lost. A detector that can find the centre of a cut-off target (the ring fit, CEN-13) reports a box that lies inside the image, such as the ring it fitted | First sim flight: the track was confirmed on the bullseye coming into view at the image's edge, 1.7 m off, and the 95th percentile at 15 m was 0.63 m against 0.30 m. The visible part's centre is wrong the same way frame after frame, so no measurement noise describes it and averaging makes the filter sure of a wrong place. Using such boxes weakly was tried and dropped: they would keep a track CONFIRMED and fresh (FND-07's rule for descending) while saying nothing about where the target is. The cost: with the 5 m sim bullseye and a box detector the track is lost below about 6.5 m, where the target stops fitting in the 640 x 360 image; `delivery/estimator` uses a 1.5 m bullseye so all three acceptance heights can be measured |
| 2026-11-18 | FND-06 | A detection within 2 m of a track of its class is that target (`SAME_TARGET_RADIUS_M`): inside the gate it updates the track; outside the gate it counts toward the five rejections that move the track; if the track already took a detection in that frame it is ignored. Only a detection further than 2 m from every track of its class starts a new track | The spec's "five gated-out measurements reset the track" does not say which track a gated-out detection belongs to. One line per finished feature, gate run or stop, newest first: `- YYYY-MM-DD <ID> DONE: <one line>`, `- YYYY-MM-DD G0: PASS ...`, `- STOP YYYY-MM-DD: <what is needed>`.
